overview: Task runner I built in TypeScript to handle async workflows with dependency chains, concurrency limits, and automatic retries. It ships with a React dashboard that connects over WebSockets so you can watch tasks run and retry failures in real time. Available on npm as @itss4nty/flowrunner.
challenges: Cascading skips when a parent fails
Keeping the dashboard in sync over sockets
Shipping a React app inside an npm package
features: Dependency chaining: tasks declare a prevId so they wait for their parent to finish before running
Concurrency control: cap how many tasks run at once with a single config value
Retry with backoff: failed tasks get re-queued up to maxTries with a configurable delay between attempts
Cascade skip: if a task burns through all retries, every task downstream of it gets skipped automatically
Built-in dashboard: a React + Tailwind UI served by Koa shows live stats, a task table, search, and tag filtering
Retry from the browser: click a failed task in the dashboard and it re-runs along with its dependents
Programmatic API: call getStats(), getAllTasks(), or reRunTask() to integrate with your own tooling

architecture.system: Four core classes + an embedded React dashboard
architecture.details: FlowRunner is the entry point: it wires up TaskScheduler, TaskStateManager, and DashboardGateway. Adding a task registers it in the state manager and enqueues it in the scheduler. The scheduler checks if there's a free concurrency slot and whether the task's dependency has completed before firing it off. If a task fails it gets retried with backoff; if it runs out of attempts the scheduler walks the dependency graph and skips everything downstream. Every state change pushes events through DashboardGateway, which is a Koa server hosting the React dashboard plus a Socket.IO layer for live updates. The dashboard can also send a retry event back, which triggers _reRunTask and recursively re-queues the whole dependent chain.
